title: Leek and Potato Soup
subtitle: silky, mild, and warming
excerpt: Leeks and potato make one of the most comforting soup combinations in British cooking. Blended smooth with a little cream, it is mild enough to be a weeknight staple. Served cold, the same recipe becomes vichyssoise.
sourceNotes: A British and French classic. The cold version, vichyssoise, was created in New York in the early 20th century by a French chef. The warm version has long been a home-cooking staple across Britain.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze before adding cream. Add cream after reheating.
recipe.batchNotes: Doubles well. Good for batch cooking and freezing in portions.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keeps in the fridge for 4 days. Reheat gently.

content.text: Wash the leeks well. Grit hides between the layers and will ruin the texture of the finished soup. Split each leek lengthways and rinse under cold running water.

items.prepNote: white and pale green parts only, sliced

content.text: Melt the butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the onion and leeks. Cook gently for 10 minutes until soft but not coloured.
Add the potatoes and stock. Bring to a simmer and cook for 20 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Blend until smooth. Stir in the cream.
Season with salt and pepper. Reheat gently if needed and serve.

items.fix: Blend in shorter bursts and serve immediately. Reheat gently -- do not re-blend.
Always split and rinse leeks before using.
Stir in extra hot stock or water until the consistency suits you.

content.text: Leek and potato soup is one of the most-made soups in Britain. It uses ingredients that are cheap, available all winter, and easy to store. The leek is also the national vegetable of Wales, giving it an extra cultural significance. Serve it warm in winter or chill it for a summer starter.
